brief: A three-storey cabinet with at least three drawers.

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases stacked at cell (0,0) on levels 0, 1 and 2 (piece:0,0,0 / 0,0,1 / 0,0,2), with snaps between them.
Three drawers (drawer:0#0,1#cut, drawer:1#0,1#cut, drawer:2#0,1#cut), one on each storey, each set into a half-north base at (0,1) levels 0-2 next to the column.

check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear; capOpenFaces closed the open faces and lockJoints bolted the joints (LOOSE_BODY cleared). Strength of the printed material is not verified by the configurator.

finish.summary: Built a three-storey cabinet: a 3-high column of hex bases at the centre cell, with a half-base drawer bay beside it on each storey carrying one drawer each (three drawers total). Open faces are capped and joints bolted; the configurator reports no issues and clear meshes. Estimated print is about 3 kg of filament and roughly 74 hours by the budget readout, so it is a large print. No props were added since the brief did not ask for them.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
